analyze.summary: Fund-safety ENFORCEMENT is strong and honest: dry-run is the default, live orders are short-circuited to "simulated" in OrderManager, live-mode startup gates (maker/allowance/balance) and the risk engine (daily-loss, exposure, position, open-order, concurrency, cooldown, kill-switch/emergency-stop) all raise/halt before real orders, emergency-stop + kill-switch are wired and authenticated (401 + CSRF, verified in EVIDENCE), and the dashboard has NO code path to set ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING or edit env.txt. Two real gaps against the spec: (1) the explicitly-named "MOST IMPORTANT REQUIREMENT" — the LIVE READINESS panel — is materially incomplete: TradingReadiness reports only 6 of the ~14 mandated checks (missing geographic availability, market active, market accepting orders, strategy loaded, risk-halt/limits, explicit CLOB-connectivity, and the ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING flag itself), is computed once at engine startup and never refreshed, so live_ready is derived over an incomplete set and the panel could read "LIVE READY = YES" while geography/market/strategy/risk conditions are unmet; (2) the committed live systemd unit does NOT set ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false — the "env.txt cannot arm live trading" guarantee holds on the running box only because the deployed unit was hardened out-of-band (per EVIDENCE), and a redeploy from this source would silently lose that belt-and-suspenders control. No fabricated data was found; the readiness gate is honest about what it checks and is currently conservative (NO). Component marked FAIL because the spec's most-important requirement is not fully met, though no funds are presently at risk given the enforcement gates and the hardened running unit.

findings.phase: Phase 5 / Phase 17 / final safety list (MOST IMPORTANT REQUIREMENT)
findings.title: LIVE READINESS panel checks only 6 of the ~14 mandated requirements
findings.spec_requirement: LIVE READINESS panel must check ALL of: CLOB connectivity, authentication, wallet, deposit wallet, USDC balance, allowance, trading enabled, market active, market accepting orders, strategy loaded, risk checks, geographic availability, live trading flag — and return LIVE READY only when every mandatory requirement passes, listing exact blockers otherwise.
findings.observed: polybot/wallet/readiness.py TradingReadiness.evaluate() populates only six checks: authentication, not_closed_only, maker_wallet, usdc_allowance, deposit_wallet_enabled, usdc_balance. live_ready is computed as `not missing` over ONLY those six (readiness.py:135). Absent entirely: geographic availability (no geo/region check exists anywhere in the codebase — grep for geo/region/country/geoblock finds only error-string handling in scripts/live_execution_audit.py), market active, market accepting orders (market_feed.py has an accepting_orders field but readiness never consults it), strategy loaded (startup loads/aborts on it in main.py:198-205 but it is not reported in readiness), risk checks / halt state, explicit CLOB connectivity as its own verdict, and the ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING live-trading flag itself. The report is produced once at engine startup (polybot/main.py:190) and the dashboard readiness card (dashboard/static/app.js:491-517, dashboard/engine_view.py:58-74) merely renders the readiness.json file as-is and never recomputes or augments it, so it is also a stale startup snapshot for the time-varying items (market active/accepting).
findings.evidence: polybot/wallet/readiness.py:52-154 (six checks; live_ready=not missing at :135); polybot/main.py:182-196 (evaluate() called only during startup()); dashboard/engine_view.py:58-74 (reads state/readiness.json, no recompute); dashboard/static/app.js:491-517 (renders checks/missing verbatim); grep confirms no geographic/market-active/strategy-loaded/risk/ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING entries in the readiness report.
findings.gap: Because live_ready is derived over an incomplete check set, the panel can report LIVE READY = YES while geographic access is blocked, no market is active or accepting orders, the strategy failed to load, or the risk engine is halted; the spec's most-important safety verdict is therefore not authoritative.
findings.proposed_fix: Extend TradingReadiness (or add a live dashboard-side aggregator that also reads engine heartbeat/registry) to evaluate and report every mandated requirement as its own check with an explicit blocker string: CLOB reachable (dedicated health() probe), geographic availability (probe CLOB from the live region / catch 403 geoblock), each configured market's active + acceptingOrders (from market registry / gamma), strategy loaded (from startup_info), risk-engine not halted and limits configured, and the ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING flag state. Compute live_ready over the full set and re-evaluate on a schedule (not just at startup) so time-varying items are current.

findings.title: Committed live systemd unit does not set ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false; env.txt-cannot-arm guarantee is not in source
findings.spec_requirement: ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false cannot be bypassed; live trading cannot be armed via env.txt while the unit forces the flag off.
findings.observed: deploy/systemd/polybot-live.service (lines 21-24) sets only Environment=PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 plus a comment stating the flag is deliberately left unset so env.txt is the control knob ('Live trading stays OFF until you deliberately set ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=true in env.txt'). deploy/install.sh:99-103 copies the unit verbatim (only path/User/Group sed substitutions), so it never injects the flag. Because load_env_file uses override=False (polybot/config/settings.py:37,57), the process-env override only protects when the UNIT sets ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false; with the committed unit it does not, so a value in env.txt (or an inherited export) directly determines enable_live_trading. Per EVIDENCE the RUNNING VPS unit and /proc/<pid>/environ DO contain ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false, i.e. the deployed unit was hardened out-of-band and no longer matches this source.
findings.evidence: deploy/systemd/polybot-live.service:21-24; deploy/install.sh:99-103; polybot/config/settings.py:37,57 (override=False) and :252 (_get_bool('ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING', False)); EVIDENCE.md lines 22-24 (running unit hardcodes false).
findings.gap: A reinstall/redeploy from this source, or any resync of the unit file, silently removes the process-env override; thereafter editing env.txt to ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=true would arm live trading (subject only to the startup allowance/balance gates), and a dashboard 'start live' would then launch a funded session. The audited safety guarantee lives only in manual VPS state, not in version control.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `Environment=ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false` to deploy/systemd/polybot-live.service (and bot-s1.service if retained) so the process env always overrides env.txt, matching the hardened running configuration; keep env.txt=true as an additional, not sole, requirement — or gate live arming behind an explicit second file/flag the unit controls.

findings.title: Dry-run enforcement chain from config to order submission is correct
findings.spec_requirement: The live trading flag must be read in config and enforced on the order path so no real order is submitted unless explicitly armed.
findings.observed: enable_live_trading is read once (settings.py:252, default False) and exposed via the dry_run property (settings.py:207-210). It is passed to OrderManager as dry_run=s.dry_run (main.py:248). In dry-run, OrderManager._submit short-circuits to order.simulated=True / status LIVE and never calls exchange.place_order (manager.py:173-184); _cancel_market, cancel_order, poll, recover and cancel_all are all guarded by _dry_run (manager.py:237,254,280,377,413). Startup logs and records the mode honestly (main.py:88-98).

findings.title: Live-mode startup gates (maker/deposit wallet, allowance, balance) abort before any order is signed
findings.spec_requirement: Live trading must be blocked when the wallet is not authorized / not funded / lacks allowance.
findings.observed: In live mode, MakerWalletValidator.validate raises MakerWalletError (maker.py:143-148, self._live) and AllowanceManager.verify raises AllowanceError via _fail (allowance.py:124-133, self._live), each caught in main.py (124-127, 171-174) and re-raised as StartupError; balance failure also aborts in live mode (main.py:135-140). main() converts StartupError/ConfigError to exit code 2 with no components wired, so no order path exists (main.py:436-445). These match EVIDENCE (usdc_allowance ok=false, deposit_wallet_enabled ok=false, balance 0<1 → live_ready=false).

findings.title: Risk engine enforces daily-loss, exposure, position, order-count, concurrency, cooldown and global halts
findings.spec_requirement: Risk engine must gate daily loss limit, max exposure and support halts.
findings.observed: RiskEngine.check_order enforces halt (engine.py:101-102), daily loss with auto emergency_stop (105-108), per-order value (111-112), max open orders (115-116), max concurrent markets (119-123), cooldown (126-129), max position size (133-135), total exposure incl. open-order notional (137-141), and wallet funds (143-144). record_fill folds realized PnL and trips emergency_stop at the daily-loss limit (152-158). is_halted honors both the in-memory emergency stop and the on-disk kill switch (68-75). Daily-loss limit 50 matches the EVIDENCE heartbeat.

findings.title: Emergency-stop / kill-switch mechanism exists, is fail-safe, and is authenticated
findings.spec_requirement: An authenticated emergency stop / kill-switch must exist and actually halt trading.
findings.observed: The engine's _guard_loop cancels all open orders when risk.is_halted() flips (main.py:346-359); is_halted reads the kill-switch file (engine.py:71-74). The dashboard emergency_stop writes the KILL_SWITCH file first, waits, then stops the unit, so the running engine cancels its own resting orders (control.py:152-182). Kill-switch paths are consistent across writer and reader (control.kill_switch_path = engine_state(mode)/'KILL_SWITCH'; paths.py:60 kill_switch = data/<mode>/state/KILL_SWITCH; RiskEngine default settings.kill_switch_file). Endpoints /api/control/emergency-stop, /clear-kill-switch and /service require an authenticated session and pass _authorise_write (permission + CSRF) (server.py:531-574,680-689); EVIDENCE confirms 401 unauthenticated. Clearing the switch requires an authenticated action and a service start to resume — fail-safe (stays halted otherwise).

analyze.summary: Paper trading isolation is implemented correctly and defensibly. The paper engine is physically incapable of submitting live orders: order writes are wired to PaperExchange (an in-process simulator that never calls the CLOB submit path), while the only CLOB client it constructs (build_public_reader) is keyless/credential-less and used solely for read-only public market data. Wallet secrets are scrubbed from os.environ in code at two points (Settings.load mode=paper and paper/main.startup), not just via the systemd UnsetEnvironment directive, and ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING is forced false. Paper uses REAL public books but simulates fills/partials/latency/slippage/fees, and writes only to the isolated data/paper tree. Dashboard control maps logical target->fixed unit with no crossover. One WARN: the committed deploy/systemd/polybot-paper.service references /opt/polybot and User=polybot, which does not match the documented deployment (/opt/bot-s1, botuser per EVIDENCE), so the ReadWritePaths/sandbox guarantees cannot be fully verified from the mirrored source and redeploying it verbatim would break paper startup. No live-order leak path found.

findings.title: Paper engine physically cannot submit live orders (simulator adapter, keyless reader)
findings.spec_requirement: Paper engine is PHYSICALLY incapable of submitting live orders (separate exchange adapter; no auth/signing path).
findings.observed: OrderManager is wired to self.exchange = PaperExchange (polybot/paper/main.py:175, :124), not to the CLOB client. PaperExchange.place_order (polybot/paper/exchange.py:146-184) only inserts a PaperOrder into an in-memory dict and matches against real depth in match()/_match_one (:257-335); it never calls reader.place_order/post_order. The sole CLOB client is build_public_reader (main.py:40-64) constructed as client_cls(host, chain_id) with NO private key and NO API creds, so ClobExchange.place_order's create_order/post_order (clob.py:106-126) has no signer and cannot sign. The reader is passed only to MarketRegistry (main.py:123) and as PaperExchange's read delegate (main.py:125); it is never handed to OrderManager or Broker.

findings.title: Wallet secrets scrubbed from process env in code, not just in the unit
findings.spec_requirement: Verify env scrubbing at startup in code (not just the unit UnsetEnvironment); paper cannot access private keys / live API creds.
findings.observed: scrub_wallet_secrets() (polybot/config/settings.py:79-84) pops all 10 WALLET_SECRET_ENV vars (:65-77: private key, proxy address, POLY_API_* and POLY_BUILDER_*) from os.environ and forces ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false. It is invoked in code twice: inside Settings.load when mode=='paper' (settings.py:222-223) BEFORE credentials are read into the Settings dataclass (so settings.private_key resolves to ''), and again defensively at PaperTradingBot.startup (paper/main.py:110). Even a misconfigured env file pointing at live secrets is neutralised because load_env_file runs then scrub immediately pops them, and the reader is keyless regardless. Confirmed by tests test_scrub_removes_every_wallet_variable and test_paper_settings_never_carry_a_key (tests/test_paper_offline.py:186-218).

findings.title: Real public book data with simulated fills/partials/latency/slippage/fees
findings.spec_requirement: Paper uses REAL public market/order-book data but SIMULATES fills/partials/latency/slippage/fees.
findings.observed: Depth comes from the real public CLOB via websocket (main.py:_on_market_event:222-230) and a REST backstop refresh loop (main.py:263-279 -> exchange.refresh_depth:129-135 -> reader.get_order_book). Matching is fully simulated: latency gating via created_ts<=now-latency (exchange.py:264,270); partial fills via maker_fill_ratio (:294-295); slippage in ticks applied against the taker (:283-307); fees on notional via fee_bps (:324,337-350); liquidity consumed within a pass so competing orders fill in sequence (:266-321). Each behaviour is unit-tested (tests/test_paper_offline.py:104-141,163-171).

findings.title: Separate data/paper tree for db/logs/state/kill-switch; no overlap with live
findings.spec_requirement: Separate data/paper/{db,logs,state,positions,orders,trades,portfolio,risk,strategy}.
findings.observed: mode_paths('paper') (polybot/config/paths.py:46-61) roots everything at DATA_ROOT/paper: logs, state, engine.db, KILL_SWITCH, and env_file=env.paper.txt (distinct from live's env.txt). Settings defaults derive db_path/log_dir/state_dir/kill_switch from mode_paths (settings.py:191-196). The paper recorder writes settings.db_path (paper) and _restore_positions reads it read-only (main.py:81,204-217). Orders/trades/positions/portfolio/risk/strategy all live inside that single engine.db per the telemetry schema. Non-overlap is asserted by test_paper_and_live_paths_never_overlap (tests/test_paper_offline.py:221-228). EVIDENCE confirms separate data/{live,paper} trees on disk.

findings.title: Dashboard control maps logical target to a fixed distinct unit; no cross-control
findings.spec_requirement: Paper controls never call the live unit and vice versa (dashboard/control.py unit mapping).
findings.observed: unit_for (dashboard/control.py:69-74) maps paper->paper_unit, live->live_unit, dashboard->dashboard_unit from DashboardSettings, whose defaults are the three distinct .service names (dashboard/config.py:80-82,174-176). service_action/_run_systemctl build argv from the allowlisted action + resolved unit with shell=False (control.py:76-124); emergency_stop routes through service_action(mode,'stop') keeping the mode->unit binding intact (control.py:152-182). No caller string reaches a shell and there is no path where a paper request resolves to the live unit. (Only residual risk: operator could set PAPER_UNIT/LIVE_UNIT env to the same value, config-driven, defaults safe.)

findings.title: Paper imports CLOB client for read-only public data only
findings.spec_requirement: Does paper import the CLOB client only for READ-ONLY public data? Confirm paper/exchange.py has no order-submit capability.
findings.observed: build_public_reader (main.py:40-64) is the only place a real ClobClient is instantiated in the paper process, keyless/credential-less, and only its read methods are exercised (health/get_market/get_order_book/get_tick_size/best_bid_ask). PaperExchange delegates ONLY reads to the reader (exchange.py:101-135) and implements order entry/cancel/match entirely in-process (:146-358). PaperExchange.address() returns literal 'paper' (:107-108) and get_collateral_allowances returns {'paper': inf} (:247-249) — no on-chain/auth call. There is no submit/sign capability against the live venue anywhere in paper/exchange.py.

findings.title: Committed paper systemd unit paths/user diverge from documented deployment
findings.spec_requirement: The paper unit must confine writes to the paper data tree (ReadWritePaths) and match the deployed environment so sandbox guarantees are verifiable.
findings.observed: deploy/systemd/polybot-paper.service uses WorkingDirectory=/opt/polybot, ExecStart=/opt/polybot/.venv/bin/python /opt/polybot/run_paper.py, User/Group=polybot, and ReadWritePaths=/opt/polybot/data/paper. EVIDENCE.md states the real project is at /opt/bot-s1 owned by botuser, and polybot-paper.service was previously running (NRestarts=0). This means the committed unit is a template that does not match the live deployment, so the ProtectSystem=strict + ReadWritePaths isolation guarantee cannot be confirmed from source. If this file were re-deployed verbatim, paper would either fail to start (path missing) or, with strict fs protection, be unable to write its own data/paper tree. This is a deployment-drift/verifiability gap, not a live-order-leak (the failure mode is fail-closed).
findings.gap: Mirrored unit references /opt/polybot & user polybot; deployment is /opt/bot-s1 & botuser.
findings.proposed_fix: Reconcile the committed unit with the deployed one: parameterise the install path (or set it to /opt/bot-s1), correct User/Group and ReadWritePaths to the real data tree, and add the actual deployed unit to the repo so the sandbox/isolation directives are auditable and reproducible.

analyze.summary: The CLOB V2 exchange layer is correctly and honestly migrated: py_clob_client_v2 is the only functional SDK dependency across auth/clob/wallet/websocket/registry, the v2 API surface is used correctly (get_open_orders, cancel_order(OrderPayload), OrderMarketCancelParams, BalanceAllowanceParams/AssetType, OrderArgs/PartialCreateOrderOptions, create_or_derive_api_key), retry/backoff is sane with order-post deliberately NOT retried, and all wallet checks are read-only and server-authoritative (proxy/EOA aware, no doomed on-chain approve). One confirmed defect underlies the known dashboard EAGAIN: ClobExchange dispatches SDK calls to threads via asyncio.to_thread with no serialization over a single non-thread-safe SDK client, and dashboard live_sync fans them out with asyncio.gather. Minor cleanups: loose version floor in requirements.txt and a dead/misleading v1 fallback in the paper public reader. No fabricated data found; absent quotes/allowances/balances resolve to 0.0/UNKNOWN and fail safe (block live).

findings.title: ClobExchange shares one non-thread-safe SDK client across concurrent to_thread calls (root cause of dashboard EAGAIN)
findings.spec_requirement: exchange/clob.py order/book/balance methods use v2 API surface correctly; retry/backoff sane (implies safe concurrency).
findings.observed: ClobExchange._call dispatches every SDK method to a worker thread via asyncio.to_thread with NO lock (clob.py:52-61). The underlying py_clob_client_v2 ClobClient wraps a single synchronous requests.Session/connection pool, which is not safe for concurrent use from multiple threads. dashboard/live_sync.py sync_once fans out _sync_health/_sync_balance/_sync_orders/_sync_trades(/positions/value) via asyncio.gather (live_sync.py:212-220), so 4-6 SDK calls run in parallel threads against the same session, producing the observed 'request error: [Errno 11] Resource temporarily unavailable' batches at identical timestamps. The live engine avoids it only because it happens to call these methods sequentially.
findings.evidence: polybot/exchange/clob.py:52-61 (no lock around asyncio.to_thread); dashboard/live_sync.py:212-220 (asyncio.gather over authenticated sync sections); EVIDENCE.md lines 57-70 (EAGAIN fingerprint).
findings.proposed_fix: Serialize authenticated SDK access: either add a single asyncio.Lock in ClobExchange._call so all to_thread dispatches are mutually exclusive per client, or change live_sync.sync_once to sequential awaits (mirroring the engine). Lock in _call is the minimal in-lane fix and protects any future concurrent caller.
findings.gap: Dashboard live panel (balance/allowances/orders/trades) can intermittently fail to refresh and show stale values; engine source-of-truth (data/live/engine.db) is unaffected.

findings.title: requirements.txt uses a version floor, not a real pin, for the v2 SDK
findings.spec_requirement: requirements.txt pins py-clob-client-v2.
findings.observed: requirements.txt:4 declares 'py-clob-client-v2>=1.1.0'. This is a lower bound, not a pin; a future backward-incompatible 2.x release would satisfy it and could break the encapsulated v2 API surface (get_open_orders, OrderPayload, etc.). Runtime currently has exactly 1.1.0 (EVIDENCE.md line 35), so production is fine today.
findings.proposed_fix: Pin to 'py-clob-client-v2==1.1.0' (or '>=1.1.0,<2') and similarly bound eth-account/py-order-utils to avoid an unvetted major upgrade on a fresh install.

findings.title: Dead/misleading v1 fallback in paper public-reader; ClobExchange hard-depends on v2
findings.spec_requirement: No functional dependency on old py-clob-client anywhere.
findings.observed: paper/main.py:51 iterates ('py_clob_client_v2.client','py_clob_client.client') and would construct a v1 ClobClient if v2 were absent. But ClobExchange.__init__ unconditionally executes 'from py_clob_client_v2 import AssetType, OrderType' and '...order_builder.constants import BUY, SELL' (clob.py:43-44), so a v1-only environment would crash at ClobExchange construction. analyze.component: Live Account Sync + Market Data + WebSocket
analyze.summary: Market discovery, per-market data, and WebSocket resilience are strong, honest, and NOT hardcoded (real Gamma discovery filtered by configurable asset/duration, full per-market field set, exponential backoff, active-ping liveness, REST backstop). The live ACCOUNT sync path has one confirmed production defect: LiveAccountSync.sync_once fans out 4-6 authenticated SDK calls via asyncio.gather, each dispatched with asyncio.to_thread onto a SINGLE shared, non-thread-safe py_clob_client_v2 requests session -> concurrent socket use -> the observed repeated [Errno 11] EAGAIN. The engine never hits this because its loops (poll 5s / book 10s / heartbeat 15s) are spaced and internally sequential. Secondary honesty gap: live account numeric fields default/persist as fake 0.0 (balance, portfolio) and [] (orders/trades/positions) rather than an explicit UNKNOWN/N/A on failure or before first successful fetch; only aggregate status flags (error_count, last_error, sections_failed, balance_ts) signal degradation. Concurrency fix is minimal and low-risk.

findings.title: dashboard live_sync EAGAIN: concurrent gather over a shared non-thread-safe CLOB SDK session
findings.spec_requirement: WebSocket for real-time, REST for reconciliation; sane concurrency; no rate-limit abuse; temporary failure never becomes fake zero; fault tolerance.
findings.observed: LiveAccountSync.sync_once runs _sync_health/_sync_balance/_sync_orders/_sync_trades (+_sync_positions/_sync_value on slow cycles) concurrently under asyncio.gather. Each ClobExchange method dispatches the blocking SDK call via asyncio.to_thread onto the ONE shared py_clob_client_v2 client (self._c), whose underlying requests/urllib3 session is not thread-safe. Multiple worker threads touch the same socket simultaneously -> [Errno 11] Resource temporarily unavailable (EAGAIN). _sync_balance itself issues 2 sequential SDK calls, so a fast cycle spawns 4-5 concurrent threads, matching the observed 'batches of 2-4 at identical timestamps' every ~70-80s. The live ENGINE issues the same calls without error because main.py's loops (order_poll 5s, book_refresh 10s, heartbeat 15s) are spaced and each awaits sequentially, so simultaneous SDK dispatch is rare. This CONFIRMS the EVIDENCE.md concurrency-collision hypothesis. WS user events also call self._wake.set() in _on_user_event, so account activity triggers extra early sync cycles, amplifying the collision rate under load.
findings.evidence: dashboard/live_sync.py:212-220 (asyncio.gather of the _sync_* coroutines); dashboard/live_sync.py:270-273 (_sync_balance: two sequential get_collateral_balance/get_collateral_allowances); dashboard/live_sync.py:117-119 (single shared ClobExchange/self._auth.client wrapped once); polybot/exchange/clob.py:52-61 (_call -> asyncio.to_thread(fn,...) on shared self._c); dashboard/live_sync.py:194-200 (_on_user_event sets _wake -> extra sync cycles); polybot/main.py:330-344 + config/settings.py:152-154 (engine loops spaced & sequential).
findings.gap: Concurrent thread access to a single non-thread-safe SDK client.
findings.proposed_fix: Serialize authenticated SDK dispatch. Minimal/low-risk: in sync_once replace asyncio.gather with sequential awaits (each section keeps its own try/except so failures still degrade only that section). Robust root-cause fix (also hardens the engine against the same latent race): add a per-instance `self._lock = asyncio.Lock()` in ClobExchange and wrap the `await asyncio.to_thread(fn,*args)` in `_call` with `async with self._lock:` so the shared client is never used by two threads at once. RetryPolicy(attempts=3) currently masks most collisions but wastes calls and floods logs.

findings.title: Live account fields show fake 0.0 / empty instead of UNKNOWN on failure or before first fetch
findings.spec_requirement: Live wallet/account fields come from real APIs; missing field => N/A; API failure => UNKNOWN (never fake 0).
findings.observed: _empty_state() initialises balance=0.0 and every portfolio figure (cash/positions_value/total_value/unrealized/realized/total_pnl/exposure) to 0.0, and open_orders/trade_history/positions to []. On a section failure, sync_once catches the exception via gather(return_exceptions=True), increments error_count/last_error, but leaves the field at its last value (or the initial 0.0/[]). So a persistently failing _sync_balance (e.g. during the EAGAIN storm) or a not-yet-run sync presents balance $0.00 and $0.00 PnL that are indistinguishable from genuine zeros. The value itself carries no UNKNOWN/N/A sentinel; only aggregate status (status.error_count, status.last_error, status.sections_failed, status.api_ok, and wallet.balance_ts which is only set on success and is absent in _empty_state) signal staleness, which the value fields do not reflect. This violates the strict 'never fake 0 / show UNKNOWN' requirement, though partially mitigated by the freshness/status metadata.
findings.evidence: dashboard/live_sync.py:452-473 (_empty_state defaults 0.0 / []); dashboard/live_sync.py:221-233 (failures only bump counters, values untouched); dashboard/live_sync.py:270-282 (balance_ts set only on success, absent from _empty_state); dashboard/live_sync.py:321-355 (_recompute_derived emits numeric 0.0 portfolio regardless of freshness).
findings.gap: No per-field UNKNOWN sentinel or freshness gate on the live account values themselves.
findings.proposed_fix: Track per-section last-success timestamps (health/balance/orders/trades/positions) and expose a per-section 'stale'/'unknown' flag; render None (mapped to UNKNOWN/N/A in the UI) instead of 0.0/[] when a section has never succeeded or last succeeded before the current auth session / beyond a staleness cutoff. At minimum add balance_ts, orders_ts, trades_ts, positions_ts to _empty_state and have the frontend show UNKNOWN when ts==0.

findings.title: Market discovery is real (Gamma) and NOT hardcoded to BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP condition IDs
findings.spec_requirement: Market discovery: not hardcoded; discovers active markets; NO ACTIVE MARKET when none.
findings.observed: MarketFeed.discover() pages real active/unclosed/unarchived markets from Gamma (/markets ordered by startDate desc, limit=100, up to 10 pages, graceful stop on offset-too-large), then classifies each by asset keyword (word-boundary regex) and duration inferred from the slug window or from real start/end timestamps (not slug text alone). BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP and 5m/15m are configurable FILTERS (DASHBOARD_ASSETS/DASHBOARD_DURATIONS), not hardcoded market identifiers; settled windows (end_ts<=now) are dropped; markets are ordered by soonest-resolving and capped at max_markets_tracked. When none match, snapshot() returns markets:[] with count:0 and a discovery block (last_ts, error, tracked, limit) — honest emptiness, not fabricated. Note: the live ENGINE (main.py) trades an operator-configured MARKETS=<condition_id> list (aborts if empty), which is env-driven config, not source-hardcoded; discovery is the dashboard's responsibility and is implemented correctly.

findings.title: WebSocket resilience: exponential backoff, subscription resume, active-ping liveness, no reconnect on idle
findings.spec_requirement: WebSocket real-time with reconnection, sane intervals, exponential backoff, stale-data indicators.
findings.observed: ClobWebSocket reconnects on any drop with exponential backoff (1s -> capped max_backoff 30s), re-sends the subscription payload on every (re)connect, and distinguishes a quiet-but-alive socket from a dead one: on recv timeout it actively pings and counts a returned pong as liveness, only forcing reconnect if a ping is unanswered within stale_timeout (45s). It exposes status (connected, last_message_ts, age_s, reconnects) as a stale-data indicator, and one bad event never kills the socket. The engine runs separate market + user channels; live_sync uses the user channel only as an early-refresh trigger with REST as source of truth, so a dropped socket degrades to polling, not to stale data.
findings.evidence: polybot/exchange/websocket.py:73-139 (run/_serve backoff, subscription resume, active-ping liveness); polybot/exchange/websocket.py:63-71 (status/age_s); dashboard/live_sync.py:10-15,194-200 (WS as trigger, REST authoritative).

findings.title: Timeouts, retry with jittered exponential backoff, and non-retried order posting
findings.spec_requirement: Fault tolerance: timeouts, retry, backoff; no duplicate live orders on lost responses.
findings.observed: retry_async implements attempts with exponential backoff (factor 2) plus +/-25% jitter and a max_delay cap, with retry_on/give_up_on classification. RestClient (httpx, native async) sets per-request timeouts and classifies HTTP errors: 401/403 and other 4xx are fatal (no retry), 429/5xx and transport/timeout errors retry with backoff. ClobExchange retries read/cancel calls but deliberately posts orders with RetryPolicy(attempts=1) across the create_order->post_order two-step, so a lost response after a landed order is never duplicated. Discovery/book/candle loops all wrap failures and continue (discovery/candle 'must never die'). REST book snapshot bounds its burst to 40 tokens.

findings.title: Account data coverage: orders, partial fills, trades, positions, portfolio, PnL, fees, exposure, allowances, status
findings.spec_requirement: Account data: open/pending/filled/cancelled orders, partial fills, trade history, positions, portfolio value, realized/unrealized/total PnL, fees, exposure, exchange/API/WS status, last sync time.
findings.observed: live_sync reads real data via the authenticated SDK and data-API: open orders (with filled_size/remaining_size/filled_pct = partial-fill detail), trade history (capped 500, with fee resolved from absolute fee or bps rate), positions (via data-api /positions for the funder), balance and per-spender allowances, portfolio value (data-api /value), and derives locked/available/buying_power, positions_value, total_value, unrealized/realized/total PnL, exposure, open_order_notional and fees_paid. Separately, EngineView surfaces the engine DB's own order status buckets (open/filled/cancelled/rejected/pending), fills, trades, positions, equity series and PnL as the persisted source of truth (survives engine stop). findings.title: Zero completed trades render fabricated 0% / 0.0000 analytics instead of N/A
findings.spec_requirement: Trade analytics computed ONLY from completed trades; 0 completed trades => "N/A" not "0%".
findings.observed: With no completed trades (EVIDENCE: trades(0) in both live & paper DBs), trade_stats() returns _empty_trade_stats() with win_rate=0.0, loss_rate=0.0, average_trade=0.0, average_win=0.0, average_loss=0.0, expectancy=0.0, expectancy_pct=0.0, largest_win=0.0, largest_loss=0.0. The Analytics tab then renders 'Win rate 0.00%', 'Loss rate 0.00%', 'Average trade 0.0000', 'Expectancy 0.0000' etc. F.pct(0.0)='0.00%' and F.signed(0.0)='0.0000' (0 is not null so the '—' guard is bypassed). This falsely implies a 0% (all-losing) win rate rather than 'no data'. Mitigating: ratio metrics that ARE None (profit_factor, sharpe, sortino, calmar, avg_r, risk_reward) correctly show '—', and KPI subtitles show '0 trades' / '0W / 0L'.
findings.evidence: dashboard/analytics.py:79-90 (_empty_trade_stats returns 0.0 for win_rate/loss_rate/average_trade/expectancy); dashboard/static/app.js:976,986-995 (F.pct(t.win_rate), F.signed(t.average_trade/expectancy)); dashboard/static/app.js:44,50,51-55 (F.num/F.pct/F.signed treat 0 as a real value, not '—').
findings.proposed_fix: In _empty_trade_stats() (and the len(pnls)==0 path) return None instead of 0.0 for win_rate, loss_rate, average_trade, average_win, average_loss, expectancy, expectancy_pct, largest_win, largest_loss. The front-end already renders None as '—' via F.pct/F.num/F.signed, so no JS change is required. net_pnl/total_fees may remain 0.0 (genuinely zero).
findings.gap: Front-end null-safe already; only the empty-stats defaults need to become None.

findings.title: Strategy panel shows invented "Accuracy" metric and 0.00% win rate the strategy does not provide
findings.spec_requirement: Strategy panel shows ONLY fields the strategy actually exposes; if the strategy lacks confidence/stop-loss/take-profit/accuracy => "NOT PROVIDED BY STRATEGY", never invented.
findings.observed: engine_view.strategies() manufactures an 'accuracy' field set equal to win_rate (stats.get('win_rate',0.0)) and defaults win_rate/accuracy to 0.0 when the strategy has no completed trades. The compiled CheapBuyStrategy (base.Strategy contract in polybot/strategy/base.py) exposes no accuracy/win-rate concept at all. The Strategy card then renders 'Win rate 0.00%' and 'Accuracy 0.00%' for the single running strategy (EVIDENCE: strategy_state(1), zero completed trades) — an invented metric showing a fabricated 0%. This value is also carried in the 1 Hz snapshot via summary()->strategies(), so it is live-visible. (Confidence is handled honestly: shows 'not published' when null; stop/target show '—' when the strategy doesn't set them.)
findings.evidence: dashboard/engine_view.py:200-207 ("win_rate": stats.get("win_rate", 0.0), "accuracy": stats.get("win_rate", 0.0)); dashboard/engine_view.py:248 (strategies() included in per-mode summary snapshot); dashboard/static/app.js:823-824 (stat('Win rate', F.pct(strategy.win_rate)); stat('Accuracy', F.pct(strategy.accuracy))); polybot/strategy/base.py:83-114 (Strategy contract has no accuracy/confidence/SL/TP).
findings.proposed_fix: Drop the duplicated 'accuracy' field (or render it as 'not provided by strategy'), and default win_rate/average_win/average_loss/total_pnl/profit_factor to None (not 0.0) when the strategy has no completed trades (stats absent). Front-end F.pct(null) already yields '—'; for accuracy specifically render a literal 'not provided' label like the confidence field.

findings.title: Candle/OHLCV source not labelled in the dashboard UI
findings.spec_requirement: Candle/price SOURCE clearly labeled (e.g. "Polymarket midpoint", "reconstructed"); never imply Polymarket supplied OHLCV.
findings.observed: Candles are honestly reconstructed from the up-outcome order-book midpoint sampled each interval (OHLC = min/max/last of mid), with volume from observed WS trade prints — this is documented in the module docstrings. But the Markets tab presents a full OHLCV-style indicator grid (EMA/RSI/MACD/ATR/VWAP/Bollinger/ADX/Volume Δ) and a candle chart with only a 'Mid' series label and no visible note that Polymarket publishes no OHLCV and these bars are reconstructed. A user could reasonably assume exchange-supplied candles. (Not a fabrication — the underlying data is real; the gap is labelling.)
findings.evidence: dashboard/indicators.py:1-13 (docstring: 'Polymarket does not publish OHLCV ... builds candles itself from the mid price'); dashboard/market_feed.py:11-12,473-499 (_sample_candles builds OHLC from mid_price, volume from trade prints); dashboard/static/app.js:711-774 (market card: indicator grid + chart, hint line 773 omits candle source); dashboard/static/app.js:677-685 (chart series labelled only 'Mid').
findings.proposed_fix: Add a hint on the market card / candle chart, e.g. 'Candles reconstructed from Polymarket order-book midpoint (no exchange OHLCV); volume from observed trade prints.' No logic change.

findings.title: Sharpe/Sortino annualised (×√365) from as few as 2-3 daily samples
findings.spec_requirement: Sharpe/Sortino require enough samples; no annualizing minutes of data.
findings.observed: equity_stats() correctly buckets equity samples to UTC days before computing returns (so it never annualises minutes — good), and returns None when <2 daily returns exist. But it will compute and annualise a Sharpe/Sortino by ×√365 as soon as there are just 2 daily returns (i.e. 3 distinct calendar days of samples), which is far too few for a meaningful annualised ratio and can produce wildly large/misleading values. The UI hint also states the ratios appear 'until at least two days of samples exist', whereas the code needs 3 distinct days for a ratio. Currently benign at runtime (equity spans <3 days => shows '—'), but the gate is thin.
findings.evidence: dashboard/analytics.py:144-159 (if len(daily) >= 2: ... sharpe = mean/sd*sqrt(365)); dashboard/analytics.py:198-209 (_daily_returns => N-1 returns for N distinct days); dashboard/static/app.js:1017 (hint: 'until at least two days of samples exist').
findings.proposed_fix: Raise the minimum daily-return count before emitting Sharpe/Sortino (e.g. require >=20 daily returns, or gate on span_days>=~30), and correct the UI hint to match the actual threshold.

findings.title: Volume/VWAP/Volume-Delta reflect only up-token trade prints
findings.spec_requirement: Indicators computed only with enough real data; sources honest (data completeness).
findings.observed: _record_trade_volume() only accumulates volume/buy_volume/sell_volume when token == market.up_token, so DOWN-outcome trade prints are ignored. Volume, VWAP and Volume-Delta therefore reflect only up-token activity. This is internally consistent (candle close/high/low are the up-token mid) and is real observed data, not fabricated — but the displayed 'Volume Δ' understates total market activity. Not a fake zero.
findings.evidence: dashboard/market_feed.py:453-461 (if ... token != market.up_token: return); dashboard/indicators.py:174-199 (vwap/volume_delta consume these partial volumes).
findings.proposed_fix: Either count both outcomes' prints (up-side equivalent) into candle volume, or label the VWAP/Volume-Δ tiles as 'up-outcome only'. Optional.

findings.title: Indicators return None (rendered '—') on insufficient data, never a fake zero
findings.spec_requirement: Indicators computed only with enough real data; else N/A, never 0.
findings.observed: Every indicator guards its window: ema/wilder_smooth return [None]*n when len<period; rsi requires len>period; macd gates the signal on len(defined)>=signal; bollinger/atr/adx/momentum/realised_volatility return None until their windows fill; compute_all returns {ready:False, bars:0} for empty candle series. _last()/_tail() propagate None, and the front-end F.num/F.price/F.pct render None as '—' (not 0). No indicator emits a fabricated 0 for a not-yet-computable window.
findings.evidence: dashboard/indicators.py:36-48,51-62,68-85,88-107,121-150,153-168,205-242,248-255,318-323; dashboard/static/app.js:44,49,50,752-771 (indicator tiles use F.num/F.price/F.pct with null->'—', volatility_pct/momentum_pct explicit '—' on null).

findings.title: Charts guard insufficient data and are lightweight with no fabricated points
findings.spec_requirement: Charts guard insufficient data with 'Not enough data'; no fabricated points; not CPU/RAM heavy.
findings.observed: charts.js is pure 2D canvas with no external libraries (CSP-friendly), caps devicePixelRatio at 2, and every mark (line/bars/histogram/hbars/donut/timeline/spark/depth) calls empty() with a caller-supplied message when data is missing; spark returns silently for <2 points. Null/non-finite values become gaps in lines (pts mapped to null and skipped) rather than interpolated fake points. Callers pass explicit empty text ('Collecting candles…', 'No completed trades yet', 'Not enough trades yet', 'No equity samples yet', etc.).

findings.title: Trade analytics derived only from completed trades; undefined ratios correctly N/A
findings.spec_requirement: Analytics from completed trades only (signals/rejected/cancelled don't count); ratios that need more history return N/A; definitions documented.
findings.observed: full_report() consumes only the engine 'trades' table (completed round trips) and the 'equity' samples; order signals/rejections/cancellations live in the separate orders table and are never counted. profit_factor, average_r_multiple, risk_reward_ratio, payoff_ratio, sharpe, sortino, calmar all return None when their denominators/samples are undefined (rendered '—'). Sortino explicitly returns None when no downside is observed. Definitions are documented in the UI (profit factor 'gross win ÷ gross loss'; 'Sharpe/Sortino annualised from daily equity returns'; volatility labelled '(ann.)').

findings.title: Strategy confidence honestly shows 'not published'; SL/TP passthrough only

analyze.summary: Dashboard auth stack is solid and honest: bcrypt(cost 12) password hashing, server-side opaque 256-bit sessions with HttpOnly/SameSite=Lax/Secure cookies, mandatory X-CSRF-Token double-check on all writes, server-enforced 3-role RBAC, per-(user|IP) login lockout, idle+absolute session timeouts, append-only audit trail with secret masking, and a required no-default secret key. Orders table exposes all 13 required real-exchange fields (with honest "—"/empty states, never fake zeros), the journal auto-records completed trades idempotently with optional non-blocking screenshots, and alert channels are correctly optional (email/telegram/discord disabled by default, missing creds never fail startup). One real gap: session revocation and session-timeout are only enforced on REST — an already-open WebSocket is authenticated once at connect and never re-checked, so a disabled/deleted/password-reset user keeps streaming live data over their open socket. Three low-severity notes (unused secret key, spoofable XFF, bcrypt 72-byte truncation).

findings.title: Open WebSocket is authenticated only at connect; session revocation and timeout are not enforced on the live stream
findings.spec_requirement: Secure sessions with idle + absolute timeout and role-based access; disabling/deleting a user or changing a password must terminate that user's access.
findings.observed: websocket_endpoint resolves the principal exactly once at accept and then loops forever on receive_json without ever re-validating the session. hub.revoke_session (which actually closes the socket) is only called from the /api/auth/logout route (server.py:251) and the self-service /api/auth/password route (server.py:275). Admin user-management paths — set_active (security.py:138), delete_user (security.py:143) and admin password reset via patch_user->change_password (security.py:159) — only call revoke_user_sessions, which deletes the DB session rows but never closes the victim's open WebSocket. Consequently a user who is disabled, deleted, or has their password reset by an admin (and any session past its idle/absolute TTL) keeps receiving live snapshot broadcasts (portfolio, engine, live-account, notification data) over the already-open socket until they voluntarily disconnect; only subsequent REST calls 401.
findings.evidence: dashboard/server.py:286-312 (WS resolves once, no re-check); dashboard/server.py:640-656 (patch_user has no hub.revoke_session); dashboard/security.py:133-144,156-159,261-262 (revoke_user_sessions = DB delete only); dashboard/hub.py:68-73 (revoke_session closes sockets, but is not called from admin paths).
findings.gap: Streaming channel bypasses session lifecycle enforced everywhere else.
findings.proposed_fix: In the WS receive loop periodically re-run security.resolve(sid) (e.g. each broadcast tick or every N seconds) and close with 4401 if it returns None; and call await hub.revoke_session for each affected sid from set_active/delete_user/admin password-reset (or call hub.revoke_user_sessions). Minimal, low blast-radius since the plumbing (hub.revoke_session) already exists.

findings.title: DASHBOARD_SECRET_KEY is required and length-validated but never used cryptographically
findings.spec_requirement: Secret key management for secure sessions.
findings.observed: config.py hard-fails startup if DASHBOARD_SECRET_KEY is absent or <32 chars and masks it in redacted(), and the docstring claims 'a missing session secret is a hard failure'. But sessions are opaque random tokens stored server-side and CSRF tokens are also server-side stored; grep shows secret_key is only read/validated/masked, never fed to any signer, HMAC, or cookie-signing routine. It is effectively dead config. This is not a vulnerability (server-side sessions are stronger than signed cookies) but the requirement/behaviour is misleading.
findings.evidence: grep secret_key -> only dashboard/config.py:17,69,157,166,227-233 and run_dashboard.py:43; no consumer. Sessions minted via secrets.token_urlsafe in dashboard/security.py:212-213; CSRF compared via stored value in security.py:247-249.
findings.proposed_fix: Either wire secret_key into something real (e.g. sign the session cookie as defense-in-depth) or downgrade the docstring/env comment to state it is a reserved/forward-compat value so operators are not misled about what protects their sessions.

findings.title: X-Forwarded-For is trusted unconditionally when behind_proxy, without a trusted-proxy allowlist
findings.spec_requirement: Behind-proxy handling; audit logs and login rate-limit must attribute the correct client IP.
findings.observed: client_ip() takes the first token of X-Forwarded-For verbatim whenever behind_proxy=True (default). A client able to reach the app directly could spoof XFF to poison the IP recorded in the audit trail and to evade the IP component of login lockout. In the deployed topology this is mitigated: the app binds 127.0.0.1 behind nginx (per EVIDENCE), and lockout also keys on username, so account lockout still functions. Flagged only because there is no trusted-proxy check.
findings.evidence: dashboard/server.py:157-162 (returns forwarded.split(',')[0] with no proxy validation); lockout query keys on username OR ip in dashboard/security.py:173-182.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate that request.client.host is a trusted proxy before honouring XFF, or use Starlette's ProxyHeadersMiddleware with an explicit trusted-hosts list.

findings.title: bcrypt silently truncates passwords beyond 72 bytes while the API advertises up to 256 characters
findings.spec_requirement: Password hashing with a strong algorithm.
findings.observed: hash_password uses bcrypt (good, cost 12), but bcrypt ignores bytes past position 72. password_problem and the LoginBody/PasswordBody models accept up to 256 characters, so two distinct >72-byte passwords sharing the first 72 bytes are treated as identical. Low practical impact given the 12-char minimum, but the advertised 256-char ceiling is misleading.
findings.proposed_fix: Pre-hash with SHA-256 before bcrypt (base64 the digest) to remove the 72-byte cap, or cap password length at 72 bytes in password_problem and document it.

findings.title: Password hashing uses bcrypt (cost 12) with timing-equalized login
findings.spec_requirement: Password hashing (which algo?).
findings.observed: Passwords hashed with bcrypt at cost factor 12; verification via bcrypt.checkpw wrapped to fail closed on malformed hashes. Login always runs a bcrypt comparison against a module-level dummy hash when the user is missing, so absent-user and wrong-password take the same time (no user enumeration). Password policy enforces >=12 chars and >=3 character classes.
findings.evidence: dashboard/security.py:291-317 (hash_password bcrypt gensalt rounds=12, _DUMMY_HASH, password_problem); dashboard/security.py:194-200 (constant-time login path).

findings.title: Server-side opaque sessions with HttpOnly/SameSite/Secure cookie flags
findings.spec_requirement: Secure sessions; cookie flags (HttpOnly/SameSite/Secure).
findings.observed: Session ids are 256-bit secrets.token_urlsafe tokens stored server-side (nothing decodable client-side; instantly revocable). Login cookie is set HttpOnly=True, SameSite=Lax, Secure=cookie_secure (default True), Path=/, Max-Age=session_ttl. Security headers (CSP, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS under TLS/proxy) applied globally.

findings.title: CSRF protection: mandatory X-CSRF-Token on every state-changing request, compared constant-time
findings.spec_requirement: CSRF protection.
findings.observed: Every non-safe method requires the session's CSRF token in the X-CSRF-Token header, verified with hmac.compare_digest against the server-stored per-session token; a cookie alone is never sufficient. Enforced both in the require() dependency factory and in _authorise_write for data-dependent routes. Frontend attaches the header on all non-GET/HEAD requests.

findings.title: Role-based access enforced server-side with last-admin protection
findings.spec_requirement: Role-based access.
findings.observed: Three roles (admin/trader/viewer) with an explicit permission map checked server-side per route via Principal.can(); the UI only hides, it is not the control. Live vs paper control require distinct permissions (control.live/control.paper). set_role/set_active/delete_user refuse to demote/disable/delete the last remaining admin.

findings.title: Both idle and absolute session timeouts enforced on session resolution
findings.spec_requirement: Session timeout (idle + absolute).
findings.observed: resolve() revokes the session when now > expires_ts (absolute TTL, default 12h) or when now - last_seen_ts > idle timeout (default 2h), otherwise touches last_seen_ts. Expired sessions are deleted, not just rejected. purge_expired and prune also clean session rows. (Note: enforced for REST; see DASHSEC-W1 for the WebSocket gap.)
findings.evidence: dashboard/security.py:225-245 (resolve absolute+idle checks), 269-270 (purge_expired); dashboard/config.py:70-71 (ttl 43200 / idle 7200); dashboard/db.py:214 (prune sessions).

findings.title: Login lockout / rate-limit per username-or-IP
findings.spec_requirement: Login lockout / rate-limit.
findings.observed: After max_attempts (default 6) failed attempts within the lockout window (default 300s) for a given username OR IP, further logins are rejected with HTTP 429 and a remaining-seconds message; failed attempts are recorded to login_attempts and successes are excluded from the count. Attempts recorded even during lockout.

findings.title: Append-only audit trail on privileged actions with secret masking
findings.spec_requirement: Audit logs.
findings.observed: Every privileged/state-changing action (login/logout, password change, user CRUD, service control, emergency stop, kill-switch clear, backup, export, reconnect, notification test, journal edits) writes an audit row with actor, role, action, target, detail, ip, ok; detail is passed through mask_secrets. The audit table is INSERT-only in code (no UPDATE/DELETE except retention prune at 90 days).
findings.evidence: dashboard/security.py:275-285 (audit INSERT + mask_secrets); dashboard/server.py:238,252,276,415,473,495,544,560,573,581,604,637,654,666 (audit calls); dashboard/db.py:61-72,206 (audit schema + 90d prune).

findings.title: Secret masking on config, audit detail, log/journal tails, and notification bodies
findings.spec_requirement: Secret masking / secrets exposure.
findings.observed: mask_secrets redacts 64-hex keys and keyed secret=value patterns (secret/passphrase/password/token/api_key/private_key) and is applied to audit detail, served log tails, journal tails, and notification bodies. Config.redacted() replaces secret fields with 'set (N chars)'. EVIDENCE confirms served HTML and endpoints leak zero secrets, and credentials are read from env.txt not exposed to the dashboard.
findings.evidence: dashboard/security.py:327-354 (mask_secrets, mask_address); dashboard/config.py:16-19,264-272 (_SECRET_FIELDS, redacted); dashboard/server.py:437,444 (masked tails); dashboard/notifications.py:80 (masked body); EVIDENCE.md:29.

findings.title: Orders table exposes all required fields from real exchange records
findings.spec_requirement: Orders table fields: Order ID, Time, Market, Direction, Price, Quantity, Status, Filled %, Remaining, Fees, Execution time, Exchange response, Error — from real exchange info.
findings.observed: engine_view.orders selects real engine/exchange columns (exchange_order_id, ts_created, market, side/action, price, size, filled_size, avg_fill_price, fees, status, last_error, exchange_response, execution_ms) and derives remaining_size and filled_pct honestly. The UI renders exactly these 13 columns plus Type/Avg-fill; execution_ms and exchange_response render '—' when null (not fabricated), and the empty table shows 'No orders recorded' rather than fake zeros — consistent with the observed 0 orders across all DBs.

findings.title: Trade journal auto-records completed trades idempotently; screenshots optional and non-blocking
findings.spec_requirement: Trade journal auto-records COMPLETED trades with required fields; screenshots optional and never block trading.
findings.observed: journal.sync imports rows from the engine's completed-trades table (INSERT OR IGNORE on UNIQUE(mode,trade_id)) with market, strategy, qty, entry/exit price+ts, duration, pnl, entry/exit reason and confidence; the sync runs in the dashboard's housekeeping loop, fully decoupled from the trading engines, so it cannot affect order execution. Screenshots are user-optional, validated (image data-URL only, 2 MB cap, base64-checked) and stored path-traversal-safe under uploads; user annotations are never overwritten by re-import.
findings.evidence: dashboard/journal.py:44-73 (idempotent auto-import), 142-171 (screenshot validation + safe path); dashboard/db.py:87-113 (journal schema, UNIQUE(mode,trade_id)); dashboard/state.py:142-160 (housekeeping loop, separate from engines).

findings.title: Alerts: browser notifications always on; email/telegram/discord optional and never a startup failure
findings.spec_requirement: Alerts for listed events; email/telegram/discord OPTIONAL; missing creds => not configured, not a startup failure.
findings.observed: Browser/dashboard notifications require no config and are always enabled; the listed events are covered (fill, order_rejected/failed, risk_halt, startup_failed, shutdown, cancel_all, trade_closed, profit_target, stop_loss, low_balance, allowance_issue, high cpu/mem/disk, ws disconnect, engine_stale, api_failure, service_failed). Email/Telegram/Discord default disabled; validate() only demands creds when a channel's *_ENABLED flag is true, so absent creds never fail startup. channel_status honestly reports each channel enabled/off (UI shows 'off'), and per-channel delivery failures are isolated (asyncio.gather return_exceptions) and never block the alert loop.
findings.evidence: dashboard/notifications.py:37-46 (event map), 66-96 (emit always broadcasts browser), 248-270 (isolated delivery), 331-343 (channel_status); dashboard/config.py:126-141,240-245 (channels default off, conditional validation); dashboard/static/app.js:1526-1534 (per-channel on/off/error display).

results.reason: Independently reproduced from source. The WS endpoint (dashboard/server.py:292) resolves the principal exactly once at connect and then loops on receive_json (server.py:304-306) with no re-validation; _handle_ws_message (server.py:715-725) only serves ping/subscribe/snapshot, so broadcasts (hub.py:84-94) keep flowing with zero session re-check. The only socket-closing call, hub.revoke_session (hub.py:68-73), is invoked from exactly two routes — logout (server.py:251) and self-service password change (server.py:275) — confirmed by grep. Admin-initiated revocations (set_active security.py:138, delete_user security.py:143, admin password reset via patch_user->change_password security.py:159, patch_user server.py:640-656) all funnel to revoke_user_sessions (security.py:261-262), which is pure 'DELETE FROM sessions' and never touches the hub. Idle/absolute TTL is enforced only in resolve() (security.py:236-241), which the WS never re-runs, so expired sessions also keep streaming. Result: a disabled/deleted/password-reset user, or any session past its TTL, keeps receiving live portfolio/engine/live-account/notification snapshots over the already-open socket until they voluntarily disconnect, while all subsequent REST calls correctly 401. WARN (not higher) is correct: dashboard binds 127.0.0.1 only, the WS surface is strictly read-only (no order/control actions), and the two most common revocation events already close the socket — residual risk is information continuation on one channel, not control or remote exposure. Proposed fix is sound and low-risk since hub.revoke_session plumbing already exists.

analyze.summary: Database isolation, WAL, read-only dashboard access, schema correctness, and dashboard-side retention (candles/notifications/sessions/audit/login) are all implemented correctly and match runtime evidence. The one real gap: the per-engine telemetry DB (data/{live,paper}/engine.db) has NO retention at all — the equity table (appended every ~15s) and the events table grow unbounded; prune() only covers the dashboard DB. Practical disk-fill risk is low on the 80GB VPS (~200MB/yr/engine), so this is a WARN, not a blocker, but the spec explicitly requires equity-sample and event retention and it is entirely unimplemented. Minor: no index on `strategy` (spec lists it, but no query filters by it) and no VACUUM to reclaim space after deletes.

findings.title: Engine telemetry DB (equity samples + events) has no retention — unbounded growth
findings.spec_requirement: Retention/rotation so the 80GB disk cannot silently fill; DB growth bound must include equity samples and events.
findings.observed: polybot/telemetry/recorder.py appends one equity row every equity_interval_s (default 15.0s, publisher.py:25,124-136) via INSERT OR REPLACE keyed on ts=now_s() (recorder.py:247-255), and appends events (recorder.py:269-271), but the EngineRecorder writer thread never deletes/prunes anything. The only prune() in the codebase (dashboard/db.py:202-214, invoked hourly at dashboard/state.py:153-158) operates solely on the dashboard DB tables (audit/notifications/login_attempts/candles/sessions) — it never touches data/{live,paper}/engine.db. There is no equity/events retention, no VACUUM, and no scheduled cleanup on the engine side. At 15s cadence the equity table gains ~5760 rows/day (~2.1M rows/yr) per engine and only grows; events grow with event volume.
findings.evidence: polybot/telemetry/recorder.py:162-165,247-255,269-271 (append-only, no delete); polybot/telemetry/publisher.py:25,124-136 (15s equity cadence); polybot/telemetry/schema.py:106-118,143-152 (equity/events tables, no retention DDL); dashboard/db.py:202-214 (prune covers dashboard DB only); dashboard/state.py:153-158 (prune scheduled only for self.db).
findings.gap: No mechanism bounds equity or events rows in engine.db; requirement's explicit 'equity samples, events' retention is unmet. Disk-fill risk is low today (5% used, ~200MB/yr/engine) but growth is strictly monotonic and unbounded.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a prune step to EngineRecorder run on a low cadence from the writer thread (the sole writer, so it is WAL-safe): DELETE FROM equity WHERE ts < now-N_days (or keep last K rows); DELETE FROM events WHERE ts < now-M_days. Make N/M/K configurable (e.g. EQUITY_RETENTION_DAYS, EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS). Optionally run PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)/incremental VACUUM periodically to reclaim space.

findings.title: Deletes never reclaim disk (no VACUUM/auto_vacuum) after pruning

findings.observed: No PRAGMA auto_vacuum, no VACUUM, and no incremental_vacuum anywhere. SQLite DELETEs leave free pages in the file (reused, not returned to the OS), so the dashboard DB size after prune stays at its high-water mark. This is harmless for the bounded dashboard tables (candles capped, so the file plateaus), but combined with db_arch-01 the engine.db has no delete path at all so it grows monotonically.

analyze.summary: Secret hygiene is strong: no private key / API secret / passphrase / auth token is ever logged; preflight uses non-reversible SHA-256 fingerprints and masked addresses; the paper unit strips wallet creds from the environment entirely. Per-mode log isolation is correct and enforced at the kernel level (ProtectSystem=strict + ReadWritePaths=data/<mode>), so the legacy top-level logs tree is provably inert for the running services. The real gaps are operational: in-app logging uses plain logging.FileHandler (no rotation) and deploy/install.sh installs NO logrotate config despite the docs claiming one, so a fresh install grows all per-domain log files unbounded; a 15s INFO HEARTBEAT compounds this. One minor secret-hygiene nit: the auto-generated bootstrap admin password is written in cleartext to journald.

findings.title: No in-app log rotation and no logrotate provisioned by installer (unbounded per-domain log growth)
findings.spec_requirement: Log rotation configured (in-app RotatingFileHandler or logrotate) so logs cannot silently fill the disk.
findings.observed: setup_logging() creates plain logging.FileHandler instances for errors.log and every domain file (trade/orders/strategy/execution/websocket/wallet/api). None are RotatingFileHandler/TimedRotatingFileHandler. deploy/install.sh contains ZERO logrotate references and ships no logrotate asset (find/grep both empty). Docs/CLOB_V2_MIGRATION.md:185-187 claims '/etc/logrotate.d/bot-s1: daily rotation, rotate 14, compress, copytruncate' but that file is a hand-placed system file referencing the legacy path (bot-s1) and user (botuser); it is not created or verified by the idempotent installer. A fresh install via deploy/install.sh to /opt/polybot therefore has no rotation for any of the 8 file handlers under data/{live,paper}/logs. Only the console mirror (journald) self-rotates.
findings.evidence: polybot/logging/loggers.py:102 (errors = logging.FileHandler(...)), polybot/logging/loggers.py:115 (file_handler = logging.FileHandler(...)); deploy/install.sh (no logrotate anywhere; mkdir at line 59 only); Docs/CLOB_V2_MIGRATION.md:185-187 (unbacked claim).
findings.proposed_fix: Either switch setup_logging to logging.handlers.RotatingFileHandler(maxBytes=~10MB, backupCount=5) for errors.log and each domain file, OR add deploy/logrotate/polybot to the repo and have install.sh copy it to /etc/logrotate.d/polybot (with copytruncate since the app holds handles open) referencing the real install path/user. In-app RotatingFileHandler is the more reproducible, self-contained fix.

findings.title: 15s INFO HEARTBEAT with full snapshot written every cycle to execution.log
findings.spec_requirement: Avoid excessive heartbeat logging.
findings.observed: heartbeat_loop logs self._log.info('HEARTBEAT', extra={'health': snap}) every heartbeat_interval_s (default 15.0s) via the polybot.execution logger, i.e. ~4/min => ~5,760 lines/day per engine (live + paper), each carrying the full health snapshot. It writes to execution.log (plain FileHandler, no rotation per LOG-01) and mirrors to journald. The same snapshot is already atomically published to status.json for machine consumption, making the per-cycle INFO line redundant for monitoring. This is the primary disk-fill vector when combined with LOG-01.

findings.proposed_fix: Demote the routine heartbeat to DEBUG (so it stays out of INFO files/journal), or log it only on state change / at a much longer cadence, and rely on status.json + metrics gauges for the per-cycle feed already produced at health.py:67-71.

findings.title: Auto-generated bootstrap admin password logged in cleartext to journald
findings.spec_requirement: NEVER log a password; mask credentials.
findings.observed: When no DASHBOARD_ADMIN_PASSWORD is configured, bootstrap_admin() generates secrets.token_urlsafe(18) and returns it; state.start() then logs it at WARNING: 'INITIAL ADMIN CREATED — username %r, password: %s'. This is the standard print-once pattern (the account is created with must_change_pw=True and the value is not returned when a password is configured), and install.sh documents retrieving it via journalctl. However it does write a valid, currently-active credential in cleartext to the systemd journal, where it persists until journal rotation and remains valid until the operator changes it. Strictly violates 'never log a password'.
findings.evidence: dashboard/state.py:78 (log.warning('INITIAL ADMIN CREATED — username %r, password: %s', ...)); dashboard/security.py:98-104 (generated = secrets.token_urlsafe(18); returned only when auto-generated); deploy/install.sh:152-155 (documents grep 'INITIAL ADMIN').
findings.proposed_fix: Write the generated bootstrap password to a root-only 0600 file (e.g. data/dashboard/INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD) and log only its location, or require the operator to set DASHBOARD_ADMIN_PASSWORD at install so nothing is generated. Keep must_change_pw=True.
