analyze.summary: The three-service systemd design is sound and largely meets the spec: independent polybot-live/paper/dashboard units, non-root templated User/Group, correct WorkingDirectory, WantedBy=multi-user (boot start), Restart=always, strong per-engine hardening (ProtectSystem=strict, SystemCallFilter=@system-service, minimal ReadWritePaths), resource ceilings sized to 2vCPU/4GB (total MemoryMax 2000M < 3.8Gi, total CPUQuota 190% < 200%), per-unit log separation, and comprehensive VPS monitoring (CPU/RAM/disk/network/uptimes/services/restarts/db+log sizes) with CPU/RAM/disk/service-failed thresholds wired into the alert engine. No BLOCKER/FAIL. Real defects: (1) StartLimitIntervalSec/StartLimitBurst are placed in [Service] in all three units where systemd ignores them, so the intended crash-loop cap never engages and Restart=always would restart forever; (2) source polybot-live.service does NOT encode Environment=ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false (paper does), so an idempotent install.sh re-run regenerates the unit and drops the manually-added runtime dry-run override; (3) install.sh never disables/removes the legacy bot-s1.service, leaving a less-sandboxed duplicate live unit installed; (4) no systemd-level health check (no WatchdogSec/Type=notify) so an alive-but-unhealthy process is never auto-remediated. Plus minor monitoring/deploy nits (no explicit db-unavailable alert, nginx upstream port 8787 vs deployed 8080, dashboard runs a redundant market-data collector rather than a shared read-only layer).

findings.title: StartLimit directives in [Service] section are ignored by systemd; crash-loop cap never engages
findings.spec_requirement: 3 units restart on failure with sane crash-loop handling (give up if crash-looping).
findings.observed: polybot-live.service lines 15-16, polybot-paper.service lines 16-17, polybot-dashboard.service lines 15-16 place StartLimitIntervalSec/StartLimitBurst inside the [Service] section. Modern systemd only reads these keys in the [Unit] section; in [Service] they are parsed as unknown and ignored. Combined with Restart=always + RestartSec=5-10, a genuinely crash-looping engine would restart indefinitely instead of entering 'failed' after the intended 5-6 restarts, defeating the documented intent (paper comment: 'Give up only if it is crash-looping: 6 restarts inside 5 minutes').
findings.gap: Rate-limit/backoff-cap is non-functional; no protection against a tight crash loop hammering the CPU/journal. EVIDENCE shows NRestarts=0 so this has not yet been exercised.
findings.proposed_fix: Move StartLimitIntervalSec= and StartLimitBurst= into the [Unit] section of each unit file (they may stay named StartLimitIntervalSec/StartLimitBurst). Keep RestartSec in [Service].

findings.title: Source polybot-live.service omits ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false; reinstall drops the runtime dry-run override
findings.spec_requirement: Live engine must be safe by default; deployment must be reproducible/idempotent without regressing safety.
findings.observed: deploy/systemd/polybot-live.service sets no Environment=ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING (lines 21-24 only set PYTHONUNBUFFERED and a comment claiming 'leaving it unset means a dry-run'). By contrast polybot-paper.service:24 hardcodes Environment=ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false and line 25 UnsetEnvironment scrubs every wallet credential. EVIDENCE states the *deployed* /etc/systemd/system/polybot-live.service DOES contain ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false — i.e. it was added out-of-band and is NOT in source control. install.sh:100-102 regenerates the unit from this source file on every run ('Idempotent: re-running upgrades the units'), which would silently strip that dry-run override; the live engine's safety would then depend solely on env.txt (whose contents this audit cannot see) plus load_env_file override=False.
findings.gap: Source-of-truth diverges from the hardened deployed unit; the live-trading kill default is not captured in git and is destroyed by the documented idempotent re-install. Inconsistent defense-in-depth vs the paper unit.
findings.proposed_fix: Add 'Environment=ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false' to deploy/systemd/polybot-live.service (matching the deployed unit and the paper unit) so process-env keeps overriding env.txt and reinstall is safe. Optionally add a commented UnsetEnvironment note.

findings.title: install.sh never disables/removes the legacy bot-s1.service duplicate live unit
findings.spec_requirement: Spec names the live unit bot-s1.service; assess whether the legacy disabled unit should be removed.
findings.observed: No bot-s1.service exists in the source tree (only the three polybot-*.service files). install.sh installs/enables exactly polybot-paper/live/dashboard (lines 99-118) and has no step to disable or delete a pre-existing bot-s1.service. EVIDENCE confirms bot-s1.service is still present on the VPS: disabled+inactive, but with a whole-tree ReadWritePaths=/opt/bot-s1 (less locked down than polybot-live's ReadWritePaths=/opt/polybot/data/live).
findings.evidence: deploy/install.sh:97-118; find shows only polybot-*.service in deploy/systemd/; EVIDENCE.md:17-19
findings.gap: A stale, more-privileged duplicate live unit lingers. Harmless while disabled, but an accidental 'systemctl start bot-s1' would launch a live engine that can write anywhere under /opt/bot-s1 and bypasses the newer isolation. Naming also contradicts the spec's expected unit name.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a cleanup block to install.sh: 'systemctl disable --now bot-s1.service 2>/dev/null || true; rm -f /etc/systemd/system/bot-s1.service' guarded so it only removes the legacy name, then daemon-reload. Document polybot-live.service as the canonical live unit.

findings.title: No systemd-level health check (no WatchdogSec / Type=notify / sd_notify)
findings.spec_requirement: Health checks / restart on failure for each unit.
findings.observed: All three units are Type=simple with no WatchdogSec=, no Type=notify, no sd_notify integration, and no ExecStartPre health probe (grep across deploy/ returns nothing). systemd therefore only restarts on process exit; an alive-but-unhealthy process (WS disconnected, event loop wedged, DB unreadable) is never auto-remediated by systemd. Application-level health does exist (dashboard /healthz, engine heartbeats to data/<mode>/engine.db, NotificationCenter staleness alerts), but that path notifies rather than restarts.
findings.evidence: deploy/systemd/*.service (Type=simple, no Watchdog); grep for WatchdogSec/Type=notify/sd_notify/ExecStartPre = none; dashboard/notifications.py:172-196 (app-level heartbeat staleness)
findings.gap: 'Health checks' at the supervisor level are absent; recovery from hangs is manual. Acceptable given app-level alerting, but not a true health check.
findings.proposed_fix: Optionally add WatchdogSec= to the engines and call sd_notify('WATCHDOG=1') from the engine heartbeat loop (systemd restarts if heartbeats stop). Lower-effort: keep as-is and rely on the existing engine_stale critical alert.

findings.title: No explicit 'DB unavailable' alert; engine-up-but-DB-unreadable emits nothing
findings.spec_requirement: Monitoring thresholds include 'db unavailable'.
findings.observed: EngineReader exposes availability (engine_view.py:227 'available': self._reader.available) and db.py:249-251 logs 'engine db unavailable' at debug, so the UI can show the flag. But NotificationCenter has no rule for available==false: _evaluate_engine (notifications.py:172-180) fires engine_stale only when heartbeat_age_s is not None AND > threshold. If the DB is completely unreadable while the unit is 'active', heartbeat={} and age=None, so no alert fires.
findings.gap: The 'db unavailable' condition is surfaced as a boolean but not alerted, so a silent DB failure on a running engine produces no notification.
findings.proposed_fix: In _evaluate_engine, when service.healthy and engine.get('available') is False (or heartbeat empty with a healthy unit), emit a critical 'engine_db_unavailable' alert.

findings.title: nginx upstream hardcoded to :8787 while deployed dashboard binds :8080
findings.spec_requirement: Reverse-proxy config must match the dashboard bind port.
findings.observed: deploy/nginx/polybot-dashboard.conf:15 upstream server 127.0.0.1:8787, consistent with config.py default port 8787 (config.py:61,160). EVIDENCE reports the running dashboard binds 127.0.0.1:8080 (DASHBOARD_PORT overridden in env.dashboard.txt). If nginx were activated it would 502 against 8787. Currently harmless: install.sh:121-129 installs the site but does not enable TLS/DNS, and the dashboard is 127.0.0.1-only, so nginx is not the active public surface.
findings.gap: Source (nginx+config both 8787) is internally consistent, but the deployment overrode the port without updating nginx; a future 'enable nginx' would break the proxy.
findings.proposed_fix: Either drop the env.dashboard.txt DASHBOARD_PORT=8080 override (use 8787), or make the nginx upstream port a documented variable the operator must keep in sync; note it in install.sh output.

findings.title: Dashboard runs a redundant market-data collector instead of a shared read-only layer
findings.spec_requirement: Resource efficiency: no redundant market-data collectors; prefer a shared read-only market layer; no unnecessary polling.
findings.observed: dashboard/state.py:86-88 starts three market tasks (discovery_loop, book_loop, candle_loop). market_feed.py:1-13 independently subscribes to the public CLOB market websocket, runs a REST book-snapshot backstop, and samples candles — a full second market-data pipeline parallel to each engine's own collectors. So live, paper and dashboard processes each subscribe to Polymarket market data rather than sharing one read-only layer. Cadences are modest (market_book_interval_s=1.0, candle_interval_s=15, discovery 60s per config.py:100-102) and EVIDENCE shows WS stable (reconnects=0) with headroom, so it is not currently harmful.
findings.gap: Three concurrent market-data subscriptions is the redundancy the spec cautions against; it triples upstream book/WS load and duplicates candle computation. Tolerable at current scale but not the 'shared read-only market layer' the spec prefers.
findings.proposed_fix: Longer-term: have the dashboard read candles/books the engines already persist (shared read-only layer) instead of maintaining its own WS+REST pipeline; or gate the dashboard feed off when an engine already tracks the same market. No urgent change given current load.

findings.title: PASS: three independent units, boot-enabled, non-root, correct WorkingDirectory
findings.spec_requirement: 3 separate units run independently, start on boot (WantedBy=multi-user), non-root user, correct WorkingDirectory.
findings.observed: Each unit is standalone (own ExecStart run.py/run_paper.py/run_dashboard.py), User=polybot/Group=polybot templated to the real SERVICE_USER via install.sh:100-102 sed (EVIDENCE: botuser, non-root), WorkingDirectory=/opt/polybot templated to INSTALL_DIR (/opt/bot-s1), and all carry [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target. install.sh:114-118 enables all three (live enabled but intentionally not started).
findings.gap: None.
findings.proposed_fix: None.

findings.title: PASS: resource ceilings appropriately sized for 2 vCPU / 4 GB
findings.spec_requirement: Resource limits suited to 2vCPU/4GB.
findings.observed: live MemoryMax=700M/High=520M/CPUQuota=70%/TasksMax=96; paper 600M/450M/60%/96; dashboard 700M/520M/60%/128. Total MemoryMax=2000M leaves ~1.8Gi for OS on the 3.8Gi box; total CPUQuota=190% stays under the 200% (2 vCPU) ceiling; MemoryHigh provides soft-throttle before the hard cap. EVIDENCE shows all three well within limits at runtime.
findings.gap: Minor: aggregate CPUQuota 190% is tight if all three peg simultaneously, but workload is IO/network-bound and idle in practice.
findings.proposed_fix: None required.

findings.title: PASS: strong per-engine sandboxing with least-privilege writable paths
findings.spec_requirement: Hardening; non-root; least privilege.
findings.observed: Engines set NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, PrivateDevices, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome, ProtectKernelTunables/Modules, ProtectControlGroups, RestrictSUIDSGID, RestrictRealtime, LockPersonality, RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_INET/INET6/UNIX, SystemCallFilter=@system-service (EPERM), and ReadWritePaths scoped to only data/<mode> so the read-only /opt tree cannot be modified. Dashboard deliberately relaxes NoNewPrivileges/RestrictSUIDSGID (documented, needed for sudo -n systemctl) but compensates with a narrowly-scoped sudoers allowlist (3 units x start/stop/restart) and layered ReadOnlyPaths(data/live,data/paper)+ReadWritePaths(their /state only) so it can drop a KILL_SWITCH without gaining write on the engine DBs.
findings.gap: Optional extra hardening not set (ProtectClock, ProtectHostname, ProtectKernelLogs, MemoryDenyWriteExecute, SystemCallArchitectures=native, CapabilityBoundingSet=) — enhancement only.
findings.proposed_fix: Optionally add the extra Protect*/CapabilityBoundingSet directives to the engines for defense-in-depth.

findings.title: PASS: VPS monitoring is comprehensive, read-only, and crash-isolated
findings.spec_requirement: Monitoring shows CPU/RAM/Disk/Network/uptimes(vps,bot,dash,paper)/running+failed services/restart counts/db size/log size with thresholds.
findings.observed: vps.py collects CPU percent+per-core+load1/5/15+core counts, memory+swap, disk usage+percent on the data partition (falls back to / if absent), network rx/tx rates+errors+drops+connection count, vps uptime (boot_time), dashboard process uptime, per-service state via 'systemctl show' (LoadState/ActiveState/SubState/UnitFileState/Result/ExecMainPID/NRestarts/MemoryCurrent/CPUUsageNSec) yielding healthy/failed/available/restarts/uptime_s for paper+live+dashboard, and storage() sizes for each engine DB, each engine log tree, dashboard DB and backups. Sampling runs off-loop via asyncio.to_thread on a 5s cadence and is wrapped so 'monitoring must never crash the app'. _int() correctly maps systemd's 2^64-1 'not set' to 0; _connection_count returns -1 (not a fake 0) when unprivileged.
findings.gap: Dashboard's own log size is not in storage() (it logs to journald, so N/A is acceptable).
findings.proposed_fix: None required.

findings.title: PASS: alert thresholds wired with correct directions, cooldown, and honest gating
findings.spec_requirement: Thresholds: CPU high, RAM high, disk low, service crashed, db unavailable.
findings.observed: NotificationCenter._evaluate_system fires high_cpu at cpu>=alert_cpu_pct(85), high_memory at mem>=88, high_disk at disk.percent>=90 (correct 'disk low'=high-used direction), and a critical service_failed_<name> for any unit with available && failed. Thresholds are env-overridable with sane defaults (config.py:112-123,198-206) and delivery respects per-alert cooldown. Live/engine health, allowance, low-balance, market-discovery and WS-disconnect rules add further coverage. Values are only emitted when present (None-guards), avoiding fabricated zeros.
findings.gap: 'db unavailable' is surfaced but not itself alerted — tracked separately as SYS-05 (INFO).
findings.proposed_fix: See SYS-05.

findings.title: PASS: paper unit enforces dry-run in depth and scrubs all wallet credentials
findings.spec_requirement: Paper engine must never touch live funds/credentials; separate data tree.
findings.observed: polybot-paper.service hardcodes Environment=ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false (line 24) AND UnsetEnvironment scrubs POLYMARKET_PRIVATE_KEY/PROXY_ADDRESS and all POLY_API_*/POLY_BUILDER_* secrets (line 25) as a second line of defence, with ReadWritePaths locked to /opt/polybot/data/paper only (line 43) so it cannot read or write live state. This is the defense-in-depth the live unit source is currently missing (see SYS-02).
findings.gap: None for paper; contrast documented as SYS-02 for live.
findings.proposed_fix: None; mirror this pattern into the live unit (SYS-02).

results.reason: Verified: [Service] section begins at line 7 in all three units, and StartLimitIntervalSec/StartLimitBurst appear inside it (live 15-16, paper 16-17, dashboard 15-16). Since systemd v230 these keys are only honored in [Unit]; in [Service] they are ignored as unknown keys, so the documented crash-loop caps (5/600s, 6/300s) never take effect. Combined with Restart=always + RestartSec=5-10 the intended 'give up if crash-looping' behavior is defeated. Real reliability defect; WARN is appropriate.
results.evidence: deploy/systemd/polybot-live.service:7,15-16; polybot-paper.service:7,16-17; polybot-dashboard.service:7,15-16; grep confirmed no StartLimit keys exist under any [Unit] section

results.reason: Verified: source polybot-live.service lines 21-24 set only PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 plus a comment and do NOT set ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false, whereas paper unit line 24 hardcodes it (and line 25 scrubs creds). install.sh:100-102 regenerates /etc/systemd/system units from these source files on every run (only substituting paths/user), and EVIDENCE.md:22-23 confirms the deployed live unit carries ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false added out-of-band. Reinstall therefore silently strips the deployed dry-run override, a real config-drift/reproducibility and safety-inconsistency gap. WARN correct. Note: the proposed fix of hardcoding false would also disable the documented env.txt=true arming path since process env wins over env.txt, but this does not invalidate the finding.
results.evidence: deploy/systemd/polybot-live.service:21-24; deploy/systemd/polybot-paper.service:24-25; deploy/install.sh:99-103; EVIDENCE.md:22-23

results.reason: Facts confirmed: no bot-s1.service exists in deploy/systemd (only the three polybot-*.service files), install.sh contains zero bot-s1 references and its systemd block (lines 99-118) never disables or removes a legacy unit, and EVIDENCE.md:17-19 confirms bot-s1.service persists on the VPS. However severity is overstated: the legacy unit is disabled AND inactive with NRestarts=0, and because it is not in source control install.sh causes no reproducibility regression and cannot recreate it (unlike SYS-02). Triggering harm requires a deliberate manual start of a disabled unit. This is a valid hygiene/cleanup recommendation, not a warning-level active defect; adjust to INFO.
results.evidence: ls deploy/systemd (only polybot-*.service); grep -rn 'bot-s1' deploy/ returns nothing; deploy/install.sh:97-118; EVIDENCE.md:17-19

analyze.summary: Test coverage is strong for isolation (wallet-secret scrubbing, path separation, dashboard auth/RBAC/CSRF/WebSocket) and for the allowance readiness gate, but four spec-required Phase-24 test categories are entirely MISSING: (1) the USDC balance=0 readiness/startup gate (BalanceManager.validate) is untested while the symmetric allowance gate is well-tested; (2) the consolidated TradingReadiness reporter has zero tests; (3) "API failure => UNKNOWN" for the live-account panel is never exercised (DASHBOARD_LIVE_SYNC=false in every test, so the live_sync failure path — the same code producing the known runtime EAGAIN defect — is untested); (4) "NO ACTIVE MARKET" (market_feed discovery/status) and "insufficient indicator data => N/A" (indicators.py) have no tests at all. Several present tests also carry weak data-honesty assertions (0-trades N/A, chart series, control target isolation).

findings.title: Paper cannot access live secrets — well covered
findings.spec_requirement: Test that the paper engine cannot access live wallet secrets.
findings.observed: tests/test_paper_offline.py::test_paper_settings_never_carry_a_key asserts settings.private_key=='' and settings.proxy_address=='' under paper mode even when POLYMARKET_PRIVATE_KEY/PROXY_ADDRESS are set in the environment; ::test_scrub_removes_every_wallet_variable asserts scrub_wallet_secrets() removes every WALLET_SECRET_ENV var and forces ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false; ::test_paper_and_live_paths_never_overlap asserts db/logs/state/kill_switch differ.

findings.title: Paper cannot submit live orders — covered (structurally, no explicit attempt test)
findings.spec_requirement: Test that paper cannot submit live orders.
findings.observed: test_paper_settings_never_carry_a_key asserts settings.enable_live_trading is False in paper mode; scrub forces ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false; the paper engine matches only against PaperExchange (synthetic books, no CLOB client) throughout tests/test_paper_offline.py. No single test drives 'paper tries to reach the live CLOB and is refused', but the credential+flag isolation makes a live submission unconstructible.

findings.title: No test that paper controls cannot stop live (and vice versa) at the unit/target level
findings.spec_requirement: Test that paper controls cannot stop live and live controls cannot stop paper.
findings.observed: The only control-isolation tests are RBAC (test_viewer_cannot_control_or_administer) and bad-target rejection (test_only_allowlisted_service_actions_are_accepted, which rejects target='root' and shell-injection actions). No test asserts that ControlPlane.unit_for('paper')/service_action('paper','stop') maps ONLY to paper_unit and never touches live_unit (and the reverse). Note the RBAC model does not separate the two: both 'admin' and 'trader' roles hold control.paper AND control.live (dashboard/security.py:34-41), so permission alone cannot enforce this isolation — only the target→unit mapping does, and that mapping is untested.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a test that mocks ControlPlane._run_systemctl and asserts service_action('paper','stop') is invoked with the paper unit only (and never live_unit), and symmetrically for 'live'; also assert unit_for('paper')!=unit_for('live').

findings.title: Auth, CSRF, RBAC, API endpoints and WebSocket are thoroughly covered
findings.spec_requirement: Tests for dashboard auth, authz, CSRF, API endpoints, WebSocket, database.
findings.observed: Auth: test_everything_requires_authentication, test_bad_credentials_are_rejected, test_repeated_failures_trigger_a_lockout (429), test_logout_revokes_the_session, test_session_cookie_is_httponly, test_weak_passwords_are_refused. CSRF: test_writes_without_a_csrf_token_are_refused, test_a_wrong_csrf_token_is_refused. RBAC: test_viewer_cannot_control_or_administer, test_the_last_admin_cannot_be_removed, test_privileged_actions_are_audited. API/DB: snapshot/engine/analytics/journal/export/notifications/config all read back real recorded EngineRecorder DB rows. WebSocket: test_websocket_requires_a_session, test_websocket_rejects_a_foreign_origin, test_websocket_streams_a_snapshot.

findings.title: RBAC test covers only admin vs viewer, not the 'trader' boundary
findings.spec_requirement: Test authorization boundaries for each role.
findings.observed: security.py defines three roles (admin, trader, viewer). Tests exercise admin (full) and viewer (view-only) but never the 'trader' role, whose distinguishing boundary is: has control/emergency/backup/export but NOT user administration nor control.dashboard. That boundary is untested.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a test creating a 'trader' user and asserting it can control paper/live but receives 403 on GET/POST /api/users and on control.dashboard actions.

findings.title: Chart rendering and most chart data-series are untested
findings.spec_requirement: Tests for dashboard charts.
findings.observed: Client chart code (dashboard/static/app.js, charts.js) has no JS tests, including empty-state text ('Not enough trades yet', app.js:1133). Server-side chart series are only partially covered: test_analytics asserts equity.samples and max_drawdown, but there is no test for analytics._histogram (bins/counts), the drawdown_series array, or daily-returns bucketing that the charts consume.
findings.proposed_fix: Add analytics unit tests asserting histogram bins/counts, drawdown_series shape/sign, and daily-return buckets for a known equity/trade fixture; optionally a smoke test that the /api/engine/{mode}/analytics payload contains every series the charts read.

findings.title: MISSING: 'API failure => UNKNOWN' for the live-account panel is never exercised
findings.spec_requirement: Test that on API failure the dashboard shows UNKNOWN (not fabricated zeros) — both as a Dashboard 'API failure' test and a Data-correctness 'API failure => UNKNOWN' test.
findings.observed: Every dashboard test sets DASHBOARD_LIVE_SYNC=false (tests/test_dashboard_offline.py:29), so the live_sync path is disabled. The only live_sync coverage is test_read_only_exchange_blocks_writes (write-method blocking). The failure/degradation path in live_sync.py (log.warning 'live sync unavailable' when the authenticated REST calls raise — the exact code producing the known runtime EAGAIN defect) is never driven, so nothing asserts the live_account snapshot section degrades to UNKNOWN/unavailable rather than showing stale or zeroed balances/allowances.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a test that constructs LiveSync with a ReadOnlyExchange whose methods raise, runs a sync cycle, and asserts the snapshot['live_account'] status is UNKNOWN/unavailable with no fabricated numeric fields (e.g. balance is None, not 0.0).

findings.title: Live trading remains disabled — covered
findings.spec_requirement: Test that live trading remains disabled.
findings.observed: test_startup_offline.py runs the full TradingBot.startup with ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false and asserts all placed orders are simulated (o.simulated). test_engine_offline.py drives OrderManager(dry_run=True) and asserts simulated orders. test_paper_offline test_scrub forces ENABLE_LIVE_TRADING=false and test_paper_settings asserts enable_live_trading is False.

findings.title: Readiness blocks when allowance=0 — well covered
findings.spec_requirement: Test that readiness blocks when USDC allowance=0.
findings.observed: tests/test_allowance_offline.py covers: sufficient passes+refreshes; zero allowance blocks live (AllowanceError); zero allowance only warns in dry-run (returns False); partial shortfall on one spender blocks; empty allowance map blocks; read error blocks live but not dry-run; wrong-network blocks and does not even read allowances.

findings.title: MISSING: no test that readiness/startup blocks when USDC balance=0
findings.spec_requirement: Test that readiness blocks when balance=0.
findings.observed: polybot/wallet/balance.py BalanceManager.validate() raises InsufficientBalanceError when balance<min_balance, and main.py:136-141 escalates that to StartupError in live mode (warns in dry-run). This safety gate has ZERO test coverage — the only balance test is PaperBalanceManager (paper simulation). This is an asymmetric gap: the allowance=0 gate is thoroughly tested but the symmetric balance=0 gate is not, despite runtime evidence showing usdc_balance 0.0<1.0 is a live blocker.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an offline test with a fake ClobExchange returning balance 0.0: assert BalanceManager(min_balance=1.0).validate() raises InsufficientBalanceError, and (via a startup-style harness) that live mode escalates to StartupError while dry-run only warns.

findings.title: MISSING: consolidated TradingReadiness reporter is entirely untested
findings.spec_requirement: Test that the readiness verdict blocks when balance=0 / allowance=0 / trading disabled (server-authoritative report).
findings.observed: polybot/wallet/readiness.py TradingReadiness.evaluate() (the aggregator that produces readiness.json with live_ready + missing_requirements for auth/closed-only/maker/allowance/deposit-enabled/balance) has no test. No test asserts that missing balance and allowance appear in missing_requirements, that deposit_wallet_enabled==(allowance>0), or that live_ready flips false. This is the artifact the dashboard/monitoring surface, so its honesty is untested.
findings.evidence: polybot/wallet/readiness.py:52-154; grep of tests/ shows no reference to TradingReadiness/readiness
findings.proposed_fix: Add a test driving TradingReadiness.evaluate() with a fake exchange (zero balance, zero allowances, mismatched api_key) and assert live_ready is False, each expected 'checks' entry ok flag, and that missing_requirements names the balance/allowance/deposit blockers.

findings.title: 0-trades N/A behaviour is asserted only shallowly (fake zeros not challenged)
findings.spec_requirement: Test that 0 trades => N/A (not misleading zeros).
findings.observed: test_a_stopped_engine_degrades_to_empty_not_an_error asserts summary.available is False and analytics total_trades==0, but does not assert the honesty markers: _empty_trade_stats() returns win_rate=0.0, net_pnl=0.0, average_trade=0.0 (numeric zeros) and only profit_factor/average_r_multiple/risk_reward_ratio/payoff_ratio as None. No test pins that the N/A fields are None so the UI renders '—' rather than a real 0.00; a regression turning a None into 0.0 would pass silently.
findings.proposed_fix: Extend the empty-engine test to assert analytics['trades']['profit_factor'] is None (and the other None sentinels) and that equity_stats sharpe/sortino are None on empty, documenting the N/A contract.

findings.title: MISSING: 'NO ACTIVE MARKET' / market discovery + status has no tests
findings.spec_requirement: Test that no market => NO ACTIVE MARKET.
findings.observed: dashboard/market_feed.py (discovery loop, _classify, TrackedMarket.status() returning open/closed/settling/paused/'no book', last_discovery_error handling) has no test at all. Nothing asserts that when zero markets are discovered the snapshot 'markets' section reports NO ACTIVE MARKET / empty honestly rather than fabricating a market, nor that a discovery failure surfaces an error instead of silently emptying the panel.
findings.evidence: dashboard/market_feed.py:135-146,196-254; grep of tests/ shows no market_feed/MarketFeed/discover reference
findings.proposed_fix: Add offline tests for market_feed: with an empty/failed discovery fetch, assert the markets snapshot reports NO ACTIVE MARKET (and last_discovery_error is set on failure); with a fixture book, assert status() transitions across open/no-book/settling/paused/closed.

findings.title: MISSING: 'insufficient indicator data => N/A' (indicators.py + Sharpe sample gating) untested
findings.spec_requirement: Test that insufficient indicator data => N/A.
findings.observed: dashboard/indicators.py (compute_all returns {'ready':False,'bars':0} on no candles and None per indicator when history is short, rendered as '—') has zero tests. Additionally analytics.equity_stats gates Sharpe/Sortino/volatility behind len(daily)>=2 and returns None for <2 points (analytics.py:129-159), but test_analytics uses 6 well-spaced samples and never asserts the None-on-insufficient-data path. So both indicator-level and equity-ratio 'N/A on thin data' contracts are unverified.
findings.proposed_fix: Add indicators tests: empty candles => ready False; a few candles below each indicator's window => that indicator is None. Add an analytics test with <2 equity points asserting sharpe/sortino/volatility/calmar are None while samples reports the real count.

findings.title: Strategy panel does not fabricate confidence — covered
findings.spec_requirement: Data honesty: do not invent confidence/SL/TP the strategy does not provide.
findings.observed: test_strategy_view_merges_state_and_performance asserts strategy['confidence'] is None with the comment 'the compiled strategy publishes no confidence', confirming the dashboard surfaces None rather than a fabricated value.

findings.title: Dashboard live-sync is read-only — covered
findings.spec_requirement: Isolation: the dashboard's live-account access cannot place/cancel live orders.
findings.observed: test_read_only_exchange_blocks_writes asserts ReadOnlyExchange raises AttributeError('read-only') for place_order/cancel/cancel_all/create_order/post_order; test_config_endpoint_masks_secrets and test_mask_secrets_redacts_keys_and_tokens confirm secrets are not leaked via the dashboard.

findings.title: preflight.py and live_execution_audit.py have no automated tests
findings.spec_requirement: Focus files include scripts/preflight.py and scripts/live_execution_audit.py.
findings.observed: Neither script is imported by any test; preflight is validated only by manual runtime execution (EVIDENCE: 'PREFLIGHT PASSED'). live_execution_audit.py is intentionally excluded from automated runs because it attempts real order submission (EVIDENCE lines 77-79). preflight's pure helpers (_fp, _mask_addr, _host) and its exit-code contract could be unit-tested offline without network.
findings.evidence: scripts/preflight.py:27-53,56-133; scripts/live_execution_audit.py (whole file); grep of tests/ shows no scripts import
findings.proposed_fix: Add offline unit tests for preflight helpers (_mask_addr, _host, _fp) and, with connectivity/strategy stubbed, assert the documented exit codes (3 token missing, 4 strategy fail, 6 config error). Leave live_execution_audit.py unautomated by design.

results.reason: Real coverage gap. control.py:69-74 unit_for() is the ONLY thing enforcing paper/live target isolation, since security.py:33-43 grants BOTH admin and trader control.paper AND control.live, so permission cannot separate them. No test asserts service_action('paper','stop') maps only to paper_unit (and never live_unit) or unit_for('paper')!=unit_for('live'). The existing control tests (test_viewer_cannot_control_or_administer:190-204, test_only_allowlisted_service_actions_are_accepted:227-237) only cover RBAC and bad-target/shell-injection rejection; test_emergency_stop_writes_the_kill_switch:246 uses paper only and never asserts live is untouched.
